objective: Detect and govern the portfolio system's major blind spots without confusing the existence of a control with evidence that an external outcome has occurred.
scopeBoundary: A passing run means every named blind spot has an observable control, an honest current state, and a concrete next test. It does not mean hiring effectiveness, collaborator agreement, archival completeness, or application outcomes have already been demonstrated.

hardGates.passCondition: Unmeasured hiring, collaborator, audience, and application outcomes remain explicitly unmeasured.
failureExamples: Internal eval scores are presented as recruiter validation
A planned collaborator review is described as completed

hardGates.passCondition: Every blind spot has a named observable signal, repository control, trigger, and next external or archival test.
failureExamples: A risk is discussed but cannot fail a check
A next step has no evidence target

hardGates.passCondition: Separate orchestration receipts distinguish read-only agent judgments, deterministic checks, and external human validation, while disclosing that repository provenance is auditable process evidence rather than cryptographic proof.
failureExamples: The generator certifies its own work
Two role labels are presented as two independent evaluations

hardGates.passCondition: Controls protect both record-level privacy and combination-level mosaic risk without publishing private feedback or relationship graphs.
failureExamples: Individually safe records combine into an unnecessary personal network map

anchors.1: Major known blind spots are absent.
anchors.3: Most are named but some controls are generic.
anchors.5: Every named blind spot has a distinct control and test.

anchors.1: Controls are mistaken for outcomes or uncertainty is erased.
anchors.3: Limits are present but inconsistently attached.
anchors.5: Control state, evidence state, and external outcome state remain distinct everywhere.

anchors.3: Signals exist but rely mainly on interpretation.
anchors.5: Each risk has concrete repository or field-test evidence that can change its state.

anchors.1: Controls add ceremony without reducing risk.
anchors.3: Controls help but do not target the main failure mechanism.
anchors.5: Each intervention directly addresses its blind spot with proportionate effort.

anchors.1: The system treats internal evidence as proof of external effectiveness.
anchors.3: External testing is mentioned but underspecified.
anchors.5: Unmeasured outcomes stay open and have a specific ethical field-test protocol.

anchors.1: More evidence automatically creates more public copy.
anchors.3: Selection exists but lacks a reader or argument constraint.
anchors.5: Audience, argument, claim budget, and omission are governed independently from claim maturity.

anchors.1: The portfolio can be polished indefinitely without contact with the world.
anchors.3: Next steps exist but have no trigger or evidence return path.
anchors.5: Each iteration ends in a bounded ship, solicit, apply, or learn action whose evidence returns safely.

blindSpots.risk: Internal evidence quality may not translate into fast comprehension, trust, recall, or role fit for hiring readers.
blindSpots.observableFailure: The repository claims hiring effectiveness without a dated reader study or outcome record.
requiredControls: Keep external outcome state explicit
Define a short comprehension and recall protocol
Store only aggregate public-safe findings
prohibitedSuccessClaims: Internal eval scores prove market effectiveness

blindSpots.risk: Careful partially recovered inquiries can accumulate without prioritization or closure evidence.
blindSpots.observableFailure: A partially recovered inquiry has no specific evidence target, closure condition, or disposition path.
requiredControls: Track inquiry-state counts
Prioritize high-value open questions
Name closure evidence and acceptable bounded disposition
prohibitedSuccessClaims: Every major role is fully verified

blindSpots.risk: Strong project and coalition evidence may be mistaken for complete evidence of Jamie's individual responsibility.
blindSpots.observableFailure: Coalition-level importance is projected as Jamie's individual authorship without a role-specific source relationship.
requiredControls: Decompose role hypotheses by action
Seek collaborator or contemporaneous role evidence
Keep collective and individual claims linked but distinct

blindSpots.risk: Enumerable platform traces may crowd out offline, relational, maintenance, and implementation work that left fewer machine-readable records.
blindSpots.observableFailure: Source volume or engagement counters are used as a proxy for professional importance.
requiredControls: Audit source-class balance
Open targeted leads for invisible operating work
Never rank claims by trace count alone
prohibitedSuccessClaims: The most documented project was the most important
Social volume measures Jamie's effort or impact

blindSpots.risk: A deep Knowledge Bank can produce an additive public site that makes the reader assemble Jamie's professional throughline.
blindSpots.observableFailure: A claim is activated because it matured rather than because it serves a named audience and argument.
requiredControls: Keep claim maturity separate from selection
Name audience and page argument
Use a claim budget and permit omission
prohibitedSuccessClaims: Every strong claim belongs on the site
More proof always improves the page

blindSpots.risk: Individually public-safe fragments may combine into unnecessary relationship, movement, or collaborator profiles.
blindSpots.observableFailure: Whole-graph review reveals a sensitive pattern that no single-record check detected.
requiredControls: Run periodic combination-level review
Minimize unnecessary names and network structure
Keep private feedback and raw relationship graphs outside the repo
prohibitedSuccessClaims: Publicly available means harmless to aggregate

blindSpots.risk: The system may reward compliance with its own ontology and mistake rubric integrity for truth or external usefulness.
blindSpots.observableFailure: The drafting agent is the deciding judge or independent role labels lack separate run provenance.
requiredControls: Use distinct read-only judge runs
Record judge provenance and limitations
Keep external human validation as a separate evidence class
prohibitedSuccessClaims: A deterministic check proves editorial quality
Two named perspectives equal two independent judges

blindSpots.risk: Portfolio refinement may postpone applications, conversations, collaborator review, and other contact with the world.
blindSpots.observableFailure: A substantial portfolio iteration ends without a bounded ship, solicit, apply, or learn action.
requiredControls: Declare the next external action
Time-box further polishing
Route returned evidence into the bank without publishing private feedback
prohibitedSuccessClaims: More archival work is always the highest-value next action

rules: Judges run in distinct read-only agent sessions against the same versioned evidence bundle.
The generator cannot be a deciding judge.
Judge outputs must disclose that they are LLM evaluations, not human reader research.
A deterministic checker validates structure and state; it cannot certify external effectiveness.
Keep the highest-scoring non-regressing control set and require two consecutive qualifying rounds.

stopPolicy.scoreVariancePolicy: Independent judges may differ above threshold on the same bundle. A programmatic regression is a hard gate changing from pass to fail, a criterion falling below its minimum, or calibration falling below five; smaller above-threshold score variation is not a control regression.
stopPolicy.successCondition: Both independent LLM judges pass every hard gate, score at least 92, score each criterion at least 4, score calibration 5, and repeat the pass without regression. Success applies only to blind-spot controls, not external outcomes.
stopPolicy.failureCondition: At iteration 14, preserve the strongest bounded controls and report unresolved blind spots without claiming system or external success.
